title: DNA Extraction from Swabbed Feces for Species Identification
author: Karla Vargas

steps.title: Saturate cotton applicators
steps.instruction: Immerse cotton‑tipped applicators in PBS buffer and keep them saturated for at least 3 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare lysis tube
steps.instruction: Pipette 25 µl proteinase K and 300 µl ATL buffer (Qiagen DNeasy kit) into a new, labeled 2 ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Swab scat sample
steps.instruction: Place a sheet of copy paper on a stainless‑steel tray, swab the scat surface with the PBS‑saturated applicator, cut off the applicator tip and drop it into the tube prepared in step 2.

substeps.instruction: After each sample, bleach and dry the tray, replace the copy paper, and change gloves.
Submerge scissors used to cut the applicator in 10 % bleach, rinse with water and wipe dry before cutting the next applicator.

steps.title: Incubate lysis mixture
steps.instruction: Cover tube caps with parafilm and incubate at 56 °C for 24–48 hours to allow lysis.

steps.title: Remove condensation
steps.instruction: Take off the parafilm and spin the tubes for 15 seconds to eliminate condensation inside the lids.

steps.title: Add AL buffer and incubate
steps.instruction: Using scissors or tweezers (decontaminated in 10 % bleach, rinsed and dried), remove the applicator tip, add 366 µl AL buffer, vortex briefly, and incubate at 56 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 366 µl 100 % ethanol to the tube, mix by inverting. Proceed to the next step or store the mixture at 4 °C (stable for weeks).

steps.title: Load lysate onto spin column
steps.instruction: Label a Qiagen spin column, then carefully apply 500 µl of the lysate from step 7 to the column without moistening the rim.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at ≥ 6000 × g (≈ 8000 rpm) for 1 minute as per the Qiagen DNeasy protocol.

steps.title: Collect flow‑through
steps.instruction: Discard the collection tube containing the filtrate and place the column into a new 2 ml collection tube.

steps.title: Prepare AE buffer
steps.instruction: Heat Buffer AE to 70 °C in a heat block; pipette 100 µl (or 200 µl for low‑concentration DNA) into a new tube and keep it in the heat block for later use.

steps.title: Wash with AW1
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl AW1 wash buffer to the column, centrifuge at ≥ 6000 × g (≈ 8000 rpm) for 1 minute, discard the filtrate and place the column in a new 2 ml collection tube.

steps.title: Wash with AW2
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl AW2 wash buffer to the column, centrifuge at 20 000 × g (≈ 14 000 rpm) for 3 minutes, discard the filtrate and place the column in a new 2 ml collection tube.

steps.title: Dry spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at 20 000 × g (≈ 14 000 rpm) for 1 minute to remove residual AW2, then discard the collection tube.

steps.title: Transfer column to elution tube
steps.instruction: Remove the spin column, place it into a labeled 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube and cut off the caps.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add 100–200 µl pre‑heated AE buffer directly onto the column, incubate at room temperature for 1–3 minutes (100 µl gives higher DNA concentration).

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at ≥ 6000 × g (≈ 8000 rpm) for 1 minute to elute DNA into the tube.

steps.title: Transfer DNA to storage tube
steps.instruction: Move the eluate into a labeled 0.5 ml or 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Store DNA
steps.instruction: Discard the spin column and store the DNA at 4 °C for short‑term use or at –20 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Optional second elution
steps.instruction: For maximum yield, repeat steps 16–18 once more, using a fresh 0.5 ml/1.5 ml tube or re‑using the tube from step 7; combine or keep eluates separate as desired.
